newsitem.title: USA: Ryder sells auto carrier unit to Allied for $114.5 million.
newsitem.headline: Ryder sells auto carrier unit to Allied for $114.5 million.

text.p: Truck renter Ryder System Inc. said Tuesday it has agreed in principle to sell its two units, Ryder Automotive Carrier Services Inc. and Ryder Carrier Management Corp., to Allied Holdings Inc. for $114.5 million in cash.

Ryder Carrier Services, the nation's largest carrier of cars and trucks, has 3,400 rigs in 34 states and Canada. The Troy, Mich.-based company employs 6,000 people, with revenues last year of $600 million of Ryder's total sales of $5.5 billion.

"This sale is another important step in our programme to increase shareholder value and to transform Ryder into a less asset-based company that provides value-added, intelligent solutions for its customers," said Ryder President M. Anthony Burns.

"Ryder will now be focused sharply on our long-term contractual businesses of integrated logistics, truck leasing and public transportation services, which are not cyclical and have good returns," he said.

Allied said the acquisition will expand its business with Ryder's largest customers: General Motors Corp., Ford Motor Co., Chrysler Corp., Honda Motor Co. Ltd., Mazda Motor Corp., Nissan Motor Co. Ltd., Toyota Motor Corp., Isuzu Motors Ltd., Volkswagen Group and Mitsubishi Group. The car makers are presently customers of Decatur, Ga.-based Allied.
The sale is expected to be completed before the end of 1997.
Ryder's stock was up 37.5 cents at $32.875 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange, while Allied was off 12.5 cents at $8.125 on the Nasdaq.
